subject.title: Discord DMs: inbound messages silently dropped (outbound works)

question: Should Discord account-scoped `allowFrom` keep narrowing/replacing the root allowlist, or should root and account `allowFrom` be unioned for inbound DMs?
rationale: The apparent repair can broaden who may start Discord DM agent sessions on narrowed accounts, so code inspection alone should not choose the security contract.

options.title: Preserve Account Narrowing
options.body: Keep account-scoped `allowFrom` as the default narrowing boundary and address this issue through explicit account configuration, diagnostics, or a separately approved migration.

options.title: Union Root And Account Lists
options.body: Allow root-listed users through account DMs too, which addresses the reported root-cause hypothesis but broadens access for accounts that were intentionally narrowed.

options.title: Add Explicit Inheritance Policy
options.body: Introduce a documented opt-in inheritance mode only if maintainers want both root convenience and account-specific narrowing.

recommendation.title: Preserve Account Narrowing
recommendation.body: Keep account-scoped `allowFrom` as the default narrowing boundary and address this issue through explicit account configuration, diagnostics, or a separately approved migration.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses Discord account config, shared DM access, and security-sensitive sender admission, where history and live timeline point most strongly to steipete.
